assumptions: The product remains decision support: it neither optimises gambling engagement nor makes final player-account decisions, and every automated result has meaningful human review and contestability.
An initial operator supplies lawfully authorised, representative event and intervention-outcome data; cross-operator pooling is not assumed.
Independent safer-gambling, privacy, security, and licensing specialists have real authority over the deployment boundaries.
The offline benchmark is feasible within 100000 PLN and 25 hours per week, but any live deployment must be partner-funded and staffed beyond the founder alone.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: British rules require operators not only to detect harm indicators but also to manually review automated processes, record interventions, permit challenges, and evaluate later outcomes. A versioned evidence and drift ledger fits that end-to-end obligation well, although predictive safer-gambling analytics itself is established rather than new.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: The pain is mandatory, continuous, and high consequence: poor detection or review can harm players and create regulatory exposure. Operators plausibly fund compliance and manual-review efficiency, but no reviewed source establishes willingness to buy independent validation from a small vendor or delegate this sensitive workflow.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Paid offline validation followed by annual monitored licences offers high contract value and repeat work, with a plausible 65-80% mature gross-margin range. Prices, CAC, procurement duration, implementation cost, insurance, expert support, and 12-18 month payback are unknown; reaching 30 contracts while retaining 20% EBITDA is a demanding, service-sensitive scenario.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Licensed Great Britain remote operators and their player-account platforms are a clear, economically serious beachhead with common regulatory obligations. It is also a concentrated buyer population, and the packet supplies no count or spend evidence showing that the accessible independent-tool segment supports the proposed scale.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A vendor-neutral audit, drift, and outcome-evaluation layer could occupy a narrower position than a risk-scoring engine. Playtech's BetBuddy already markets early identification and intervention support through a major platform, while operators and platforms control the data and can build or bundle the missing evidence features.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: The workflow could extend to more operators, products, platforms, and regulated jurisdictions, and continuous model assurance is reusable as a capability. Model drift, differing interventions, local regulation, and restricted data sharing limit transferability and make each expansion partly bespoke.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Versioned threshold performance, subgroup audits, and intervention outcomes can deepen within each authorised deployment. Cross-operator pooling cannot be assumed, the operator owns the most valuable data, and a platform incumbent can accumulate similar history with stronger distribution.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Interpretability, human-review evidence, out-of-time validation, and outcome measurement could improve auditability over opaque scoring alone. No benchmark demonstrates better precision-recall, subgroup safety, reviewer productivity, or regulatory acceptance than an operator's current process or BetBuddy.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Explicit customer-interaction requirements and scrutiny of significant automated decisions make monitoring, human oversight, and evidence of effectiveness timely. Licensing classification remains fact-specific, however, so regulation creates demand but not a reliable licence moat.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: A paid operator benchmark followed by one platform integration is focused and could leverage a partner's installed base. Representative data access, platform willingness, security approval, procurement time, exclusivity, and repeatable acquisition are all unresolved, and the founder lacks a pre-existing operator channel.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder is technically well matched to modelling, monitoring, and causal evaluation, and an offline prototype is feasible. Live use carries severe privacy, fairness, false-negative, false-positive, security, licensing, and conflict-of-incentive risks and is explicitly incompatible with solo part-time operation.

main_structural_strength: The regulatory workflow explicitly joins indicator detection, human review, intervention records, and outcome evaluation, creating a recurring evidence problem well matched to an interpretable analytics product.
primary_score_limiter: Validation and deployment require privileged operator data and platform cooperation in a high-stakes environment where a major incumbent already sells the central capability and the founder cannot support live operations alone.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Playtech's BetBuddy already provides predictive safer-gambling analytics and intervention support, while published studies show material indicator drift and threshold sensitivity rather than a stable universal classifier.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid operator-controlled offline study should deliver an out-of-time benchmark against the incumbent process, subgroup false-positive and false-negative results, measured reviewer hours and intervention outcomes, a written licensing-perimeter opinion and DPIA, and a platform or operator commitment with acceptable annual price, support scope, and payback.
highest_value_structural_change: Make the enduring product an operator-hosted, vendor-neutral assurance layer that audits any existing harm model, including incumbent models, for drift, subgroup performance, human review, and intervention outcomes; avoid raw-data pooling and defer proprietary real-time scoring until the assurance wedge controls distribution.
